The data above is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function  $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z>-0.86).$ Use the table above and do not round your answer.

$P(Z>-0.86)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/dc28d78d3f9334aad287ba8e3532b95e4287b84b395d58301016bb056dff2006.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>-a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>-0.86).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/07d788a65e5a5c177e7d1e54a3212c71eb0b36f22ec9f582ebb3ad37c6de8cb7.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z<0.86).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/abdde6b554257a3ed44d091a9a87095af7bde7534b0695f5ac97d6bf24bcb160.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>-0.86)=P(Z<0.86)=Φ(0.86)=0.8051.
$$
